answer: A dune field radio relay gives each agent one mast on a named dune crest, held by a buried anchor plate no hand can shift without leaving a mark. Each morning the agent turns a brass cipher disk at the mast base and broadcasts the day's code to the next relay. Two neighboring masts must log the same code within the hour or the mast goes dark for a season, and the relay keeper checks every plate against a stamped survey map each month. A thousand fake agents need a thousand masts on a thousand dune crests and a thousand cipher disks turned every morning.
